variables.claim_asserts: Large land tracts and oceans have persisted since the Silurian in the geographic regions occupied by present continents and oceans.
variables.test_measures: On a global 2-degree grid at nine reconstructed times from 440 to 50 Ma, the fractions of present land cells always reconstructed as land (L_all = 0.0007) and present ocean cells always reconstructed as ocean (O_all = 0.3377).

modality.note: GPlates MERDITH2021/PALEOMAP plate reconstructions are appropriate evidence for geographic persistence, while reconstructed coastline polygons proxy land and ocean occupancy rather than observing it directly.

assumptions.note: A 0.5 persistence threshold operationalizes 'large tracts'; requiring the same cells to retain state at every sampled time is a strict but recognizable reading of persistence from the remotest period.

scope.claim_scope: Global present continental and ocean regions continuously back to the Silurian.
scope.test_scope: Global 2-degree cells evaluated at nine discrete palaeogeographic reconstructions from 440 to 50 Ma, with known palaeolongitude and coastline-model uncertainty.

reasons: L_all and O_all directly operationalize persistence in the present geographic regions named by the claim.
The global reconstruction modality fits the claim and does not merely test a modern biological reinterpretation.
Discrete reconstructed times, coastline polygons as an occupancy proxy, and uncertain deep-time palaeolongitude make the evidentiary scope narrower than continuous historical persistence.
what_would_change_it: Denser time sampling with uncertainty ensembles and explicit palaeogeographic land/ocean probability surfaces would test continuous persistence across the full interval more faithfully.
